title: 10 best AI product video generators for e‑commerce in 2026
summary: Compare the best AI product video generators for e‑commerce, including Photoroom, Creatify, PixVerse, Topview, Runway, and more.
body_markdown:
Product video can help shoppers understand how an item moves, reflects light, fits, or looks from different angles. But producing it traditionally means organizing another shoot, coordinating people and products, editing footage, and repeating the process for every format or sales channel.


For a small e‑commerce team, that becomes expensive quickly. For a high-volume seller managing hundreds or thousands of products, it can become operationally impossible.


AI product video generators promise a faster alternative. They can turn product photos, product-page URLs, scripts, or prompts into videos for product pages, marketplaces, social media, and paid advertising.


The difficulty is choosing a tool designed for e‑commerce rather than one that simply produces impressive AI footage.


Photoroom’s[AI Product Video Generator](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator) turns existing product photos into realistic, ready-to-publish videos using more than 300 e‑commerce templates, a custom prompt, or both. Sellers can create motion assets for product pages, marketplace listings, ads, and social media channels without arranging a traditional video shoot.


The best AI product video generator isn’t necessarily the most advanced text-to-video model. For e‑commerce sellers, the strongest tools are those that can preserve the product accurately, work from existing catalog assets, produce channel-ready formats, and generate multiple videos without requiring a traditional shoot.

One note on pricing: pricing and product availability were reviewed in September 2026. Most AI video platforms use credits, generation limits, premium models, or separate API pricing, so the real cost depends on how many usable videos your business needs to produce.


## How we compared the best AI product video generators


We compared these tools using their current official product documentation, feature pages, published pricing, supported workflows, and stated e‑commerce use cases. We didn’t rank them solely on the technical sophistication of their underlying video models. Although quality is an important factor, focusing on output would overlook the practical requirements of e‑commerce production.


Instead, the comparison focuses on 9 key factors that matter most for e‑commerce teams producing product videos with AI.


### 1. Product fidelity


Is the workflow designed to keep the product’s color, proportions, materials, packaging, labels, and branding consistent?[Inaccurate colors](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/how-to-fix-inaccurate-ai-product-images) , proportions, or branding can mislead shoppers—triggering returns and poor reviews—or violate marketplace listing policies.


### 2. Existing asset compatibility


Can e‑commerce sellers begin with product photos, catalog images, product URLs, descriptions, or footage they already have? Tools that allow you to start with existing assets fit more directly into your production workflow than tools that require you to start from scratch.


### 3. Ease of production


Can an e‑commerce seller create a usable result without advanced prompting or professional video-editing experience? Most e‑commerce teams need a tool that can be onboarded quickly and produce accurate,[catalog-ready results](https://www.photoroom.com/product-catalog) without additional training.


### 4. Catalog scalability


Can the process be repeated across dozens, hundreds, or thousands of products? A tool that only works well for a handful of hero products won't hold up for sellers who need video across an entire catalog.


### 5. Output flexibility


Can the finished video can be adapted for product pages, marketplaces, paid media, and social channels? Sellers need formats that adapt to different surfaces without separate production runs.


### 6. Creative control


Does the tool offer[templates](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator/templates) , prompts, reference images, scripts, editable scenes, or model selection? More creative control lets brands match the product video style to their identity, rather than settling for generic AI output.


### 7. Workflow integration


Does video generation connect with image editing, batch production, localization, ad creation, or e‑commerce publishing? Video generation that connects to image editing and batch tools cuts down the number of platforms a team has to manage.


### 8. Commercial suitability


Are exports, usage rights, plan limits, and pricing practical for business use? Usage rights and plan limits determine whether a video can actually be published commercially, not just generated.


### 9. Fit for the intended seller


Does the tool solve a real e‑commerce production problem rather than simply demonstrating generative-video capabilities? A tool built for e‑commerce production solves a different problem than one built to showcase general video-generation capability.


## 1. Photoroom: Best overall AI product video generator for e‑commerce


Photoroom is the strongest overall option for sellers who want to turn existing product photography into realistic video without a disconnected production process.


[Photoroom’s AI Product Video Generator](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator) allows users to upload between one and four product images and choose from more than[300 e‑commerce templates](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator/templates) . Sellers can use a template for a predictable starting point, write a custom prompt for more creative direction, or combine both approaches. Videos can be generated in different aspect ratios and exported as MP4 files for product pages, marketplace listings, online stores, advertising, and social media.


The workflow is built specifically around e‑commerce product assets. Rather than asking a model to invent the product from text, Photoroom starts from the seller’s real product photography and is[designed to keep important details](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/introducing-photoroom-fidelity-layer-for-image-editing) —including color, texture, shape, and branding—consistent through the generation.


Video generation sits within Photoroom’s wider product-content workflow. A seller can[remove](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/background-remover) or[replace a background](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/instant-backgrounds) ,[improve lighting](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/image-brightener) ,[correct the source image](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/edit-with-ai) ,[create additional product visuals](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/product-staging) , and[turn the finished asset into video](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator) without moving between several applications.


**Ideal user:** Photoroom's AI Video Generator is particularly useful for two audiences:


-


A founder or marketing lead at a small or medium-sized brand who treats[product visuals as a direct sales lever](https://www.photoroom.com/use-cases/sell-online)


-


A professional seller[managing a large catalog](https://www.photoroom.com/use-cases/catalog-images) across multiple channels, where consistency and operational speed matter more than open-ended creative experimentation


### Photoroom pros


-


Built around e‑commerce products rather than generic AI scenes


-


Works with product photography sellers already have


-


Includes more than 300 product and virtual-model video templates


-


Supports templates, prompts, or a combination of both


-


Accepts up to four reference images for additional visual guidance


-


Designed to maintain important product details


-


Produces MP4 assets in multiple aspect ratios


-


Connects video generation with background removal, product-image editing, AI Backgrounds, Batch, and Virtual Model


-


Suitable for both occasional production and repeatable catalog workflows


-


Available on web, iOS, and Android


### Photoroom cons


-


Video Generator is limited to Max and Ultra plans


-


Not designed for long-form or heavily scripted video production


-


Doesn’t specialize in avatar-led or presenter-led UGC ads


-


Templates don’t provide traditional timeline-level editing of every individual element


-


Highly conceptual campaign scenes may still require a more open-ended platform such as Runway or Luma


**Choose Photoroom when:** You want to turn existing product photos into realistic, repeatable video assets and keep image preparation and video production in the same e‑commerce workflow.


## 2. Creatify: Best for turning product URLs into video ads


Creatify is an AI advertising platform. Its strongest e‑commerce workflow turns a product page into a ready-to-publish video ad.


A user can submit a product page, and[Creatify](https://creatify.ai/) extracts relevant information and assets to help create a script, scenes, voiceover, presenter, and finished video. The platform provides product-video generation, AI actors, UGC-style formats, ad templates, an inspiration library, and batch production.


**Ideal user:** Performance marketers producing ads from product URLs. Its Batch workflow can create variations from multiple product URLs, making it more suitable for paid-media production than a conventional manual video editor.


### Creatify pros


-


Converts product URLs into complete video ads


-


Can begin with images, scripts, or other visual assets


-


Includes AI actors, voiceovers, scripts, and UGC-style formats


-


Supports product-focused videos as well as presenter-led ads


-


Offers batch generation for multiple products and creative variations


-


Useful for paid-social testing and performance marketing


-


Provides a limited free plan to test the tool


### Creatify cons


-


Focuses more on complete ads than clean product-only video


-


URL extraction gives less control over which assets get prioritized


-


AI-presenter and UGC output needs brand/accuracy review


-


Less integrated with product-photo correction than Photoroom


-


Credit use rises with many variants and revisions


**Choose Creatify when:** You need to create and test many scripts, actors, and CTAs fast, starting from a product page rather than a photo.


**Choose Photoroom instead when:** You need product-led videos that can be reused consistently across listings, product pages, social content, and ads.


## 3. PixVerse: Best for complete commercial-style ads from one product image


PixVerse is a broad AI video platform with a dedicated advertising workflow called Ad Master.


[PixVerse's Ad Master workflow](https://app.pixverse.ai/mini-apps/ad-master) turns one product image and a set of selling points into a multi-scene commercial with voiceover, captions, and music—a finished ad rather than a simple animated photo.


The wider PixVerse platform supports image-to-video, text-to-video, templates, lip sync, native audio, conversational generation, node-based workflows, and other production tools.


**Ideal user:** Sellers who want a full commercial built automatically from one image.


### PixVerse pros


-


Builds a full ad from one image and selling points


-


Auto-generates scenes, voiceover, captions, music, and supporting creative


-


Needs less shot-by-shot planning than open-ended video tools


-


Combines a dedicated ad workflow with broader video generation


-


Supports image-to-video, text-to-video, templates, native audio


-


Provides options for APIs and more advanced production workflows


-


Transparent per-video and API pricing


### PixVerse cons


-


Ad Master gives the AI substantial creative control


-


App and API use separate subscriptions/credit balances


-


Broad feature set may exceed what a small seller needs


-


Generated scenes, people, and product interactions need additional review


-


Fine details (text, labels, jewelry, fasteners) need testing before scaling


**Choose PixVerse when:** You want AI to turn a product photo and selling points into a complete commercial-style advertisement.


**Choose Photoroom instead when:** You want the existing product image to remain the central asset and need video editing to connect with product-image editing and catalog production.


## 4. Topview: Best for producing multiple performance-ad concepts


Topview is designed primarily for marketers creating video advertisements rather than sellers who only need to animate catalog photos.


Users can start with a prompt, product URL, image, video, reference asset, or other campaign input.[TopView’s AI Video Agent](https://www.topview.ai/) can help develop the concept, plan scenes, generate visuals, add voice and captions, and adapt the result for channels such as TikTok, Reels, Shorts, and paid advertising.


**Ideal user:** Performance marketing teams testing different hooks, narrative structures, presenters, and messages.


### Topview pros


-


Accepts prompts, URLs, images, video, and reference material


-


Handles scripting, scenes, visuals, and edits in one workflow


-


Supports avatars, voiceovers, captions, localization


-


Adapts creative for multiple social/ad formats


-


Good for generating and testing several campaign concepts


-


Enterprise and API options for larger teams


### Topview cons


-


Centered on ads rather than clean product-gallery video


-


Broad model/workflow set needs more setup than a focused tool


-


Auto-generated scripts and claims need human review


-


Credit-based production is harder to forecast across revisions


-


Presenter-led formats may not suit premium or product-only use


**Choose Topview when:** Your paid media team is testing several hooks, scripts, or presenters before committing spend to one direction.


**Choose Photoroom instead when:** You need consistent product videos that work ads and product listings.


## 5. Pippit: Best for link-to-video and social-commerce production


Pippit is an e-commerce-oriented content platform that can turn product links, media, files, and instructions into marketing videos.


Pippet’s Video Agent supports links and uploaded assets, and its product workflows can generate scripts, captions, voices, avatars, promotional visuals, and channel-specific formats.


[Pippit](https://www.pippit.ai/) is especially relevant for social commerce. Its TikTok Shop workflow can import product pictures, video, features, and other listing details from a product link, and allows the seller to add brand information, prices, audience details, and a logo before generation.


**Ideal user:** Social-commerce sellers running TikTok Shop or similar campaigns.


### Pippit pros


-


Builds video from product links, files, images, and media


-


Generates scripts, captions, voiceovers, promotional scenes


-


Direct, purpose-built TikTok Shop workflow


-


Supports avatars, translation, multiple social formats


-


Includes editing and direct publishing


-


Free access alongside paid credit plans


### Pippit cons


-


Focused more on promotional content than product-only animation


-


Imported product info/prices need verification


-


Broad feature set can make it hard to know what to use


-


Output may need editing to match brand guidelines


-


Pricing/credits vary by market


-


Less connected to product-image correction than Photoroom


**Choose Pippit when:** Your production starts from a product link and needs to publish straight to social-commerce channels.


**Choose Photoroom instead when:** Your priority is creating accurate motion assets from prepared product photos and reusing them across multiple e‑commerce channels.


## 6. Runway: Best for premium product campaigns


Runway’s platform helps agencies and creative teams develop premium product campaigns. The platform offers more control over scenes, references, motion, style, and editing than most automated e-commerce-ad generators. That makes it appropriate for hero campaigns, launches, premium social content, and higher-value brand assets.


That flexibility can create more work. Teams that use[Runway](https://runway.com/product/ai-video-generator) need stronger prompting, art direction, iteration, and quality assurance than they would with a template-first e‑commerce tool.


**Ideal user:** Agencies and creative teams producing premium campaign visuals.


### Runway pros


-


Advanced image-to-video and generative-editing capabilities


-


Can transform and restage existing product shots


-


Offers multiple first-party and third-party video models


-


Provides substantial control over scenes, movement, lighting, and style


-


Includes upscaling and professional video-editing tools


-


Supports advanced workflows and enterprise production


-


Provides free access and several paid plans


### Runway cons


-


Requires more creative knowledge than e-commerce-first tools


-


Credit usage can climb quickly during experimentation


-


Likely to be unnecessarily complex for routine product-listing videos


-


Product accuracy depends heavily on source material, model choice, and direction


-


Collaborative plans are priced per editor


-


Doesn’t provide the same integrated catalog image workflow as Photoroom


**Choose Runway when:** You need distinctive, high-end campaign visuals and have the creative resources to direct and refine them.


**Choose Photoroom instead when:** You need a repeatable product-content workflow that non-specialists can use across the entire product catalog.


## 7. InVideo AI: Best for complete narrated marketing videos


InVideo AI is an AI-powered video product platform. Its AI’s workflows can combine product links, prompts, scripts, AI-generated footage, stock media, avatars, voiceovers, subtitles, and music to create multi-scene product explainers, ads, and social content.


InVideo’s primary strength is its breadth: a marketer can provide an idea or product and let the platform construct much of the finished piece. That breadth is less ideal for e‑commerce, where product accuracy matters most. Sellers who use[InVideo AI](https://invideo.io/) should verify that generated or stock scenes don’t imply incorrect features, materials, ingredients, use cases, or results.


**Ideal user:** Teams that want a full narrated explainer or promo assembled by AI.


### InVideo AI pros


-


Creates complete marketing videos from prompts or product information


-


Includes scripts, voiceovers, subtitles, music, and supporting media


-


Suitable for multi-scene explainers and promotions


-


Can combine AI-generated visuals with stock footage


-


Accessible to teams without traditional video-editing expertise


-


Offers free and paid subscription options


### InVideo AI cons


-


Less specialized in product-photo fidelity


-


Stock and generated media can create visual inconsistency


-


Outputs may require editing to feel specific to the brand


-


Different models and workflows consume different quantities of credits


-


Less suitable for uniform videos across a large SKU catalog


-


Source product images may need to be prepared in a separate tool


**Choose InVideo AI when:** You need a complete narrated marketing video containing the product, supporting footage, text, and voice.


**Choose Photoroom instead when:** The product needs to remain visually central and accurately represented.


## 8. HeyGen: Best for avatar-led and multilingual product videos


HeyGen is an AI avatar and presenter platform. It generates videos featuring AI spokespeople, translates and dubs them into other languages, and syncs lip movement to the new audio. These capabilities are useful for product demonstrations, UGC-style advertising, customer education, onboarding, and international campaigns.


[HeyGen](https://www.heygen.com/) may add unnecessary complexity for a product-only video. Sellers who simply want to animate a product photograph will usually have a more direct workflow in Photoroom.


**Ideal user:** Brands needing presenter-led or multilingual product content.


### HeyGen pros


-


Strong range of AI presenters and avatars


-


Supports translation, dubbing, and lip synchronisation


-


Useful for adapting campaigns to multiple markets


-


Appropriate for UGC-style and presenter-led product advertising


-


Provides individual, business, enterprise, and API options


-


Can combine presenters with generated supporting footage


### HeyGen cons


-


Adds unnecessary complexity for sellers who don't need an avatar


-


Presenter-led format doesn't fit every brand or listing


-


Premium features and higher production volumes consume more credits


-


Not built for product-gallery or marketplace-listing videos


-


Product-image preparation needs to happen in a separate tool


-


Business and team plans can be expensive for small sellers


**Choose HeyGen when:** You need the same video adapted into multiple languages, or a spokesperson on screen.


**Choose Photoroom instead when:** You need the product itself—not the presenter—to remain the focus.


## 9. Luma: Best for cinematic product experimentation


Luma is a creative image and video platform designed for visually ambitious asset generation.


[Luma](https://lumalabs.ai/create/ai-video-generator) is ideal for creating atmospheric product scenes, camera movement, transformations, dramatic lighting, and conceptual campaign ideas. Creative teams can use product imagery as a starting point and explore visual treatments that would be difficult or expensive to film traditionally.


It's best treated as a creative-exploration tool rather than an e‑commerce production tool: strong for a hero launch or a one-off concept, but less practical for repeating across a full catalog.


**Ideal user:** E‑commerce creative teams experimenting with cinematic treatments.


### Luma pros


-


Strong cinematic image-to-video generation


-


Useful for lighting, atmosphere, movement, and visual experimentation


-


Appropriate for premium social and campaign concepts


-


Supports high-resolution generation and upscaling


-


Provides paid plans suitable for commercial use


-


Useful for creative teams exploring several visual directions


### Luma cons


-


Not built specifically for e‑commerce catalog production


-


Free access may carry watermark or commercial-use restrictions


-


Requires stronger prompting and creative direction than a template tool


-


Product fidelity should be reviewed in complex generated scenes


-


Costs increase with model choice, resolution, duration, and iteration


-


Less efficient than Photoroom for routine product-photo-to-video production


**Choose Luma when:** A single hero product or launch calls for a distinctive visual style worth the extra prompting and iteration.


**Choose Photoroom instead when:** You need dependable, repeatable output across many products rather than one striking result.


### 10. Whatmore: Best for shoppable video on e‑commerce stores


Whatmore is a video e‑commerce platform. Their[Shoppable Videos](https://www.whatmore.ai/shoppable-videos/) tool helps e‑commerce brands create or import product video from social media and publish shoppable video experiences on their product pages. This is especially helpful for Shopify brands that want to add video to their product and collection pages.


Whatmore can complement a tool like Photoroom instead of replacing it. A seller could use Photoroom to create and prepare the product visual, then use Whatmore to make that video interactive and shoppable on the storefront.


**Ideal user:** Shopify brands publishing shoppable video on product pages or landing pages.


### Whatmore pros


-


Combines video content with e‑commerce publishing


-


Supports shoppable, interactive on-site video


-


Connect video directly to individual products


-


Allows brands to reuse existing creator and social content


-


Particularly relevant to Shopify stores


-


Addresses distribution and conversion, not just production


### Whatmore cons


-


Not primarily an image-to-video generator


-


Pricing is less transparent than many self-service creative tools


-


Strongest benefits depend on implementing the storefront experience


-


Not equally relevant across every marketplace


-


Works alongside, rather than replaces, a tool like Photoroom


**Choose Whatmore when:** You have existing video assets that you want to publish on your e‑commerce store.


**Choose Photoroom instead when:** You still need to create the underlying video asset before it can be made shoppable.

## How to choose the right AI video tool for your e‑commerce business


With so many AI video platforms on the market, the right choice depends less on which tool is most advanced and more on how well it fits the way your team actually works. The considerations below will help you evaluate any[AI video tool](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator) against your specific catalog, channels, and team—whether that's Photoroom or one of the alternatives covered above.


### 1. Start with the intended channel


A clean product video for a marketplace listing has different requirements from a UGC-style TikTok ad. Identify whether the video is intended for a product page, marketplace gallery, paid campaign, organic social post, email, or another placement.


### 2. Decide whether the product or the message is the focus


Product-first videos need to preserve and showcase the actual item. Message-first advertising can rely more heavily on scripts, presenters, hooks, testimonials, and calls to action.


### 3. Review the supported inputs


Some tools start from product photos. Others work from URLs, scripts, prompts, footage, or documents. To avoid creating another step in your production workflow, choose one that fits the assets your team already maintains.


### 4. Test product fidelity before scaling


Use products with difficult details, such as labels, reflective surfaces, patterned fabrics, transparent materials, jewelry settings, buckles, small accessories, or distinctive packaging. Review the entire video frame by frame. If the output[requires extensive edits](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/how-to-fix-inaccurate-ai-product-images) to details that matter to customers, that tool probably isn't ready for catalog-wide use yet—no matter how strong its overall output looks.


### 5. Determine whether templates or prompts fit your team


Templates are easier to standardize across sellers, products, and markets. Prompts offer more flexibility but can create less predictable output. If your team values speed and consistency across many products, lean on templates. If a specific campaign needs a distinct look or action, use a prompt instead. Some platforms, like Photoroom, allow for both at the same time: use[templates to standardize the output](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator/templates) , and prompts to fine tune as needed.


### 6. Calculate the cost per usable video


Include failed generations, revisions, premium models, longer durations, upscaling, watermark removal, additional users, storage, and commercial-use requirements. For many AI video generators, these functions cost extra.


### 7. Consider catalog volume


A workflow that works for ten hero products may not work for 5,000 SKUs. High-volume sellers should prioritize repeatability,[batch capabilities](https://www.photoroom.com/batch) ,[simple quality control](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/product-fixer) , predictable naming, and manageable costs.


### 8. Check aspect ratios and export formats


Confirm that the tool can produce the dimensions needed by your website, marketplaces, social channels, and advertising accounts without extensive manual cropping. Photoroom can generate videos in multiple aspect ratios so the same source photo can be exported for product pages, marketplaces, and social without manual resizing.


### 9. Evaluate the wider product-content workflow


You may also need[background removal](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/background-remover) ,[image cleanup](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/remove-object-from-photo) ,[product staging](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/product-staging) ,[resizing](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/image-resizer) ,[brand controls](https://www.photoroom.com/brand-kit) , localization, and[batch editing](https://www.photoroom.com/batch) . A tool that connects these steps—like Photoroom—can reduce production overhead.


### 10. Assess how much post-generation editing is needed


Some platforms produce a nearly finished video. Others expect users to refine scenes, timing, text, audio, and transitions manually. ### 11. Prioritize operational consistency over novelty

### 12. Use specialist platforms only where they add value
